problem: Embodied exploration agents rarely communicate what they perceive, and naive image captioning of every frame during navigation yields uninteresting, repetitive descriptions (e.g. facing a wall, near-identical consecutive views).
motivation: Natural-language descriptions make robot perception interpretable to non-expert humans and ease deployment of service robots. The agent must decide when a scene is worth describing while exploring efficiently, and no metric existed to jointly evaluate exploration and description.
key_idea: Combine a modular RL exploration navigator with a CLIP-based Transformer captioner, gated by a lightweight speaker policy (depth, object, or visual-activation thresholds) that triggers captions only for informative views, evaluated with a new episode description score (ED-S).
insight: Speaking less can be better: in Gibson, thresholded policies (e.g. D>=2.0, A>=5.0, O>=1) raise ED-S from 0.119 (always caption) to 0.250, 0.223 and 0.222, while too strict thresholds collapse coverage. Optimal loquacity depends on environment size: ~20-80% on small Gibson scenes, higher on larger MP3D scenes, where depth/object policies barely beat or match always-speak. CLIP features beat region features (CIDEr 139.4 vs 124.8 at tiny size), and web-scale captioner training improves all metrics.
method: Navigator: hierarchical policy (global goal on grid via PPO, A* planner with local goal within 1.25 m, local policy with forward 0.25 m / turn 10°) with neural occupancy mapper (ResNet-18 + UNet on RGB-D) and CNN pose estimator that corrects sensor odometry.

Exploration rewards compared: curiosity, coverage (area seen), occupancy anticipation, and impact (grid and DME pseudo-visitation counts); Impact (DME) chosen for the full system due to best AS and MP3D Acc.
Captioner: encoder-decoder Transformer on CLIP-ViT-L/14 features (Tiny/Small/Base), trained with cross-entropy then SCST, on COCO or 35.7M web+COCO images.
Speaker policy: triggers the captioner if mean depth >= D, if number of relevant objects >= O, or if mean of last-conv-block CLIP-encoder activations >= A.
ED-S metric: mean CLIP-S x IoU(nouns in captions, objects in environment via Jonker-Volgenant assignment) x %area seen; also Cov, Div, and loquacity (Loq).
Real-world deployment: LoCoBot with adjusted camera parameters, noise models in simulation training, and depth correction from prior work.

setting.backbone: Hierarchical RL navigator (ResNet-18 + UNet mapper, CNN pose estimator, PPO policies) + Transformer captioner on CLIP-ViT-L/14 (Base variant)
setting.training_data: Navigator: 5M frames on Gibson in Habitat; captioner: COCO (112k images) or 35.7M images (COCO, SBU, CC3M, CC12M, WIT, YFCC100M subset)
setting.action_space: Low-level: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10° (via global goal on map grid and local goal)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT maps and object annotations used only for training rewards/evaluation)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark (SR/SPL) reported; benchmarks are the paper's own exploration and description evaluations on Gibson/MP3D.
results: Impact (DME) gave the largest area seen (105.03 m² Gibson, 205.02 m² MP3D) and was used as navigator. The best speaker policies raise ED-S over always-speaking (0.257 vs 0.120 on Gibson; 0.196 vs 0.179 on MP3D). The captioner reaches CIDEr 149.6 on COCO with web-scale training.
limitations: Real-world deployment is only shown qualitatively in a video, with no quantitative real-world results.
Speaker policies are simple hand-thresholded heuristics whose best thresholds vary by dataset; ED-S depends on GT object annotations and simulator maps.
